chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: Tenor solo on 'They Shoot Horses, Don't They?'
summary: For the film's 1932 setting he played with Chu Berry in mind, and Shelly Manne guessed it; personnel of the soundtrack.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: [INAUDIBLE QUESTION]
That was the movie, "They [Shoot Horses, don't They?]"
[BREAK FROM #46 TO #49 ON MY COUNTER]
...(?)... You were talking about doing Chu Berry on a soundtrack.
Yes. Shelly Manne was on the date, and during one of the breaks he came over to me, and he says, "I know who you're thinking about." He had really figured out
T. Edwards - 123

who I was thinking about -- and it was Leon "Chu" Berry. Because he came along during that period, you know, with the Fletcher Henderson band, and the Cab Calloway Orchestra. A little later on I heard him on the radio and heard him at the theatre in Detroit. So the whole setting was in that period, the '32 period, so I just put myself in that frame of mind. And the conductor, Johnny Green, he was very surprised and happy, because it really did help put things in context. You remember the movie, They Shoot Horses, with Jane Fonda and Gig Young, Michael Sarazin...
[INAUDIBLE COMMENT]
It was about the dance marathons in the Thirties.
Was there any other (?) in the movie?
Oh yeah. They had a whole other band in the... In fact, they had two or three bands in the movie on film.
[INAUDIBLE COMMENT]

Well, bands that they put together. And they had a lot of fine players. Ronnell Bright was on the date, Joe Harris, Hadley Caliman, Bobby Hutcherson (he was the conductor), Harold Land was on the date. We had a lot of fine players. Teddy Buckner, the trumpet player, he was on the particular sideline thing; he wasn't on film. But
T. Edwards - 124

when it came to the recording, they only used about three of us out of the band. I think they used Thurman Green, Ronnell Bright and me. We were the only ones that they really used that had worked the sideline; we did the soundtrack also.
[INAUDIBLE COMMENT] ...lists a Terry Edwards.
Oh, got me wrong again! Right.
[LISTS PERSONNEL ON SOUNDTRACK RECORDING, BARELY AUDIBLE] The soundtrack edition(?) includes Gus Divona(?), Ronnie Lang, (?) Anderson on piano, Teddy Edwards (they got it correct)...
Correct that time.

...Manny Klein, Johnny Adino(?), Lloyd Earlier(?), Gil (?), Gil (?), Larry(?) Buckner, Ray Brown, Joe Mondragon, Ronnell Bright, Paul Smith, John (?), [INAUDIBLE NAME] and Carl (?). [REST OF COMMENTS ARE INAUDIBLE UNTIL...]
